questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About pure substances and mixtures: (1) A pure substance has a fixed composition and definite properties. (2) A homogeneous mixture has visibly different phases. (3) Air is an example of a mixture.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About physical and chemical changes: (1) Melting of ice is a physical change. (2) Rusting of iron is a chemical change. (3) Dissolving salt in water is always a chemical change.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About atoms and ions: (1) A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons. (2) A cation has more electrons than protons. (3) Isotopes of an element have different numbers of neutrons.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About chemical formulae: (1) The formula of calcium hydroxide is Ca(OH)₂. (2) The formula of sulfuric acid is H₂SO₄. (3) The formula of sodium carbonate is NaCO₃.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About balancing chemical equations: (1) 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O is correctly balanced. (2) Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl is correctly balanced. (3) 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO is correctly balanced.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About the mole concept: (1) One mole of any substance contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles. (2) One mole of O₂ molecules contains 6.02 × 10²³ oxygen atoms. (3) The molar mass of CO₂ is 44 g/mol.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About molar mass and calculations: (1) The molar mass of NaCl is 58.5 g/mol (Na = 23, Cl = 35.5). (2) 0.5 mol of water has a mass of 9.0 g (H₂O, Mr = 18). (3) 1.0 mol of carbon (C, Ar = 12) has a mass of 6.0 g.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About solution concentration: (1) A 0.10 mol/L NaCl solution contains 0.10 mol NaCl per litre of solution. (2) Doubling the volume of a solution without adding solute halves its concentration. (3) Concentration in mol/L is also called molarity.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About pH of strong acids and bases: (1) A 0.010 mol/L HCl solution has pH ≈ 2. (2) A 0.10 mol/L NaOH solution has pOH ≈ 1. (3) For aqueous solutions at 25°C, pH + pOH = 14.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About strong and weak electrolytes: (1) Strong acids are strong electrolytes. (2) Weak acids ionize completely in water. (3) NaCl(aq) is a strong electrolyte.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About the ideal gas law and gas volume relationships: (1) At constant temperature and pressure, gas volume is directly proportional to moles of gas. (2) At constant pressure, gas volume is inversely proportional to temperature in Kelvin. (3) At constant volume, increasing temperature increases gas pressure.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About state changes: (1) Boiling and evaporation are both liquid → gas changes. (2) Sublimation is the change from solid directly to gas. (3) Condensation is an endothermic process.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About acids and bases: (1) Acids taste sour and turn blue litmus red. (2) Bases turn red litmus blue. (3) All bases are soluble in water.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About oxides: (1) CO₂ is an acidic oxide. (2) Na₂O is a basic oxide. (3) Al₂O₃ can act as both an acidic and a basic oxide.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About salts and their solutions: (1) NaCl(aq) is approximately neutral. (2) NH₄Cl(aq) tends to be acidic. (3) Na₂CO₃(aq) tends to be basic.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About solubility and precipitates: (1) Mixing BaCl₂(aq) and Na₂SO₄(aq) forms a white precipitate. (2) Mixing NaCl(aq) and KNO₃(aq) forms a precipitate. (3) Mixing AgNO₃(aq) and NaCl(aq) forms a white precipitate.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About redox reactions: (1) In a redox reaction, oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously. (2) Oxidation involves loss of electrons. (3) A reducing agent is the species that is reduced.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About metal reactivity with acids and water: (1) Sodium reacts vigorously with cold water to produce hydrogen gas. (2) Magnesium reacts slowly with cold water but more readily with steam. (3) Copper reacts readily with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce hydrogen.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About displacement reactions of metals: (1) Zinc can displace copper from a solution of CuSO₄. (2) Copper can displace zinc from a solution of ZnSO₄. (3) Iron can displace copper from a solution of CuSO₄.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About hydrocarbons: (1) Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons. (2) Alkenes contain at least one C=C double bond. (3) Alkynes contain at least one C≡C triple bond.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About isomers in organic chemistry: (1) C₄H₁₀ can have more than one structural isomer. (2) Isomers have the same molecular formula but different structures. (3) Methane (CH₄) has two structural isomers.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About neutralization reactions: (1) Neutralization is a reaction between an acid and a base to form salt and water. (2) The reaction between HCl and NaOH is a neutralization reaction. (3) All neutralization reactions produce a neutral solution (pH = 7).

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About thermal decomposition reactions: (1) CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g) is a thermal decomposition reaction. (2) Heating CuCO₃(s) can produce CuO(s) and CO₂(g). (3) Thermal decomposition generally absorbs heat (endothermic).

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About properties of common gases: (1) Oxygen supports combustion but does not burn itself. (2) Hydrogen produces a ‘pop’ sound with a lighted splint. (3) Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About periodic trends: (1) Atomic radius generally decreases across a period from left to right. (2) Ionization energy generally increases across a period from left to right. (3) Elements in the same group have exactly the same atomic radius.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About valence electrons and groups: (1) Group 1 elements have 1 valence electron. (2) Group 17 elements have 7 valence electrons. (3) Group 18 elements are very reactive because they have 8 valence electrons.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About ionic bonding: (1) Ionic bonds usually form between metals and non-metals. (2) In NaCl, sodium loses one electron to chlorine. (3) Ionic compounds often have high melting points.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About covalent bonding: (1) Covalent bonds form by sharing electron pairs between atoms. (2) H₂O and CH₄ are examples of covalent molecules. (3) All covalent substances are gases at room temperature.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About intermolecular forces: (1) Hydrogen bonding is a strong type of intermolecular attraction. (2) Hydrogen bonding can occur between H₂O molecules. (3) Intermolecular forces do not affect boiling points.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About reaction rate: (1) Increasing temperature generally increases reaction rate. (2) Increasing concentration of reactants generally increases reaction rate. (3) A catalyst increases reaction rate by increasing activation energy.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About collision theory: (1) Reacting particles must collide to react. (2) Effective collisions require sufficient energy. (3) Effective collisions require proper orientation of particles.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About chemical equilibrium: (1) At equilibrium, the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal. (2) At equilibrium, the concentrations of reactants and products are always equal. (3) Equilibrium can be established in a closed system.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About Le Châtelier’s principle: For the reaction: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) + heat (1) Increasing pressure favours the formation of NH₃. (2) Increasing temperature favours the reverse reaction. (3) Removing NH₃ shifts equilibrium to the right.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About equilibrium constant Kc: (1) Kc is defined in terms of concentrations of reactants only. (2) A large Kc value indicates products are favoured at equilibrium. (3) Changing temperature can change the value of Kc.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About strong and weak acids: (1) A strong acid ionizes almost completely in water. (2) A weak acid has a lower degree of ionization in water. (3) A dilute acid is always weak.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About electrolytes and non-electrolytes: (1) Electrolytes conduct electricity when dissolved in water. (2) Glucose solution is a strong electrolyte. (3) Molten NaCl can conduct electricity.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About laboratory safety: (1) Safety goggles should be worn when heating chemicals. (2) Eating and drinking in the lab are allowed if hands are clean. (3) Broken glassware should be reported and handled properly.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About heating substances in a test tube: (1) The open end of the test tube should be pointed away from people. (2) The test tube should not be tightly closed when heating. (3) The test tube should be heated evenly by moving it through the flame.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About methods of separation: (1) Filtration can separate an insoluble solid from a liquid. (2) Distillation can separate liquids with different boiling points. (3) Chromatography can separate different coloured pigments in ink.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About gas tests: (1) Hydrogen gives a ‘pop’ sound with a lighted splint. (2) Oxygen relights a glowing splint. (3) Carbon dioxide turns limewater from colourless to milky.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About titration (conceptual): (1) Titration can be used to determine the concentration of an acid. (2) An indicator is often used to detect the end point of a titration. (3) The volume of solution added from the burette is not important in titration calculations.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About common laboratory apparatus: (1) A burette is used to deliver accurate volumes of solution. (2) A pipette is used to measure a fixed volume accurately. (3) A beaker is more precise than a volumetric flask for measuring volume.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About the Haber process (ammonia synthesis): (1) Nitrogen and hydrogen are the reactants in the Haber process. (2) An iron catalyst is used to increase the rate of reaction. (3) Lower temperature always gives the highest rate of ammonia production.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About the Contact process (sulfuric acid production): (1) Sulfur dioxide is oxidized to sulfur trioxide in the Contact process. (2) A vanadium(V) oxide catalyst is used. (3) Sulfuric acid is produced by directly dissolving sulfur trioxide in water in one step without any issues.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About environmental chemistry (acid rain): (1) Acid rain can be caused by sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. (2) Acid rain can damage buildings and statues made of limestone. (3) Acid rain has no effect on lakes and rivers.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About water treatment: (1) Filtration removes suspended solids from water. (2) Chlorination is used to kill bacteria in drinking water. (3) Distillation is commonly used in large-scale municipal water supply due to its low cost.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About everyday applications of chemistry (polymers): (1) Poly(ethene) is a polymer made from ethene monomers. (2) Many plastics are non-biodegradable and can cause environmental pollution. (3) All polymers are synthetic and none occur naturally.

questions.subject: 化学
questions.question: About energy changes in reactions: (1) Exothermic reactions release heat to the surroundings. (2) Endothermic reactions absorb heat from the surroundings. (3) Activation energy is the minimum energy required for a reaction to occur.
